Oxalidaceae.key_door: trifoliolate Oxalis + 5 petals + 10 unequal stamens + 5-part capsule

Celastraceae.key_door: project pair: Mortonia narrow-leaved cymose shrub vs Schaefferia spinescent dioecious shrub with red drupes

Elaeagnaceae.key_door: silvery scales + petal-less 4-lobed floral tube + drupe-like one-seeded fruit

Bixaceae.key_door: tuberous/palmately lobed Cochlospermum + yellow 5-petaled flower + many free stamens + woolly seeds

Koeberliniaceae.key_door: green photosynthetic thorn branches + tiny ephemeral leaves + 4-merous flower + 8 stamens + berry

taxonomy_notes: Project Oxalis names remain accepted current concepts; species-level Texas provenance remains independent, especially O. stricta.
Mortonia greggii and Schaefferia cuneifolia remain accepted and native to Texas/Mexico.
Elaeagnus angustifolia remains accepted but is introduced in Texas.
Cochlospermum wrightii is accepted and native from southwest Texas southward; Amoreuxia wrightii is homotypic synonym provenance.
Koeberlinia spinosa is accepted and native to Texas; variety resolution remains species-lane work.
Joey routing was checked first; no direct target-family frames were indexed.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not use Oxalis flower color alone for yellow-woodsorrel species.
Do not export the Mortonia/Schaefferia project-pair morphology as a universal Celastraceae key.
Keep Russian olive explicitly introduced in Texas.
Do not identify Koeberlinia varieties from family-level thorn impressions.
